# SPD-083 — Two members cannot run the suite at once in one checkout: tests/helpers.py deletes REPO/bin/__pycache__ at exit and each run reads the other's in-flight source

## Brief
Found by SPUD-050/Charlotte on 2026-09-15 while two members worked the same worktree in parallel (Eric's eleven-ticket hook batch, waves 1 and 2). Two of her full-suite runs failed spuriously: tests/helpers.py deletes REPO/bin/__pycache__ at exit, so two concurrent runs race on it, and each run imports the program from the one shared working tree, so it reads whatever the other member has half-written. Nothing is wrong with the tests themselves; the suite is simply not safe to run twice at once in one checkout.

This matters for the way Spud now works: parallel members with disjoint deliverable globs are the whole point of the fan-out, and every one of them is told to run the full suite before it returns. Today that verification is only trustworthy when one member runs at a time, which serialises the slowest step of every wave (about eight minutes) and quietly weakens the evidence behind a member's Result.

A fix wants: a lock or a wait so only one suite run at a time touches the shared bytecode directory, or a per-run scratch copy of bin/ and tests/ so each run reads a snapshot of its own; plus a decision about what a member should do when another run holds the lock (wait, or run its own subset and say so). Measure the cost of a concurrent run either way, and say in the result whether the brief template should keep telling every member to run the whole suite.

## Size, persona and model decision
One engineer on opus, no children, when picked up. Probably a lock or a per-run scratch copy of the tree; measure what a second concurrent run costs before choosing.
